oper_nm: Support for the design of the Digital Transformation Program for effective access to health care in Colombia
objtv: This technical cooperation aims to support the Ministry of Health and Social Protection in the design and implementation of the Digital Transformation Program for Effective Access to Health in Colombia. Specifically, the cooperation will focus on supporting: (i) support the Ministry of Health and Social Protection (MSPS) for the design and implementation of the digital transformation program for the Health System and ii) provide technical assistance for the development and deployment of digital mechanism to optimize the workflow for medical-claims auditing processes carried out by the Administrator of the Resources of the Social Security Health System (ADRES).

oper_nm: Strengthening integrated management of disaster risk and climate change
objtv: The general objective of the Technical Cooperation (TC) is to support the country in strengthening institutional management of climate and disaster risk. The specific objectives are: (i) to strengthen the National System for Disaster Risk Management (SNGRD) and the institutional capacity of the National Unit for Disaster Risk Management (UNGRD) for the implementation of disaster risk management (DRM) in the country; and (ii) to enhance the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit (MHCP) to improve financial management of the country's contingent liabilities related to disasters and climate. Additionally, this TC will provide technical support for the implementation of the PGIRDN of the Contingent Loan CO-O0018.

oper_nm: Support the process of integration of early childhood and youth care services in Bogotá D.C.
objtv: The objective of this technical cooperation (TC) is to support the development of comprehensive strategies to improve the provision of early childhood and youth services in Bogotá, D.C.

oper_nm: Acceleration of the Venture Capital and Impact Investment Ecosystem in Colombia
objtv: The project aims to bring together relevant stakeholders and strengthen the impact investment ecosystem in Colombia, facilitating access for ventures and initiatives with social and environmental impact to various sources of funding, including financial and technical assistance. It seeks to increase the technical and management capacities of impact-oriented companies so they can align with the standards required by investors and access specialized funds. Additionally, it will work on developing capacities for Entrepreneurship Support Organizations (ESOs), such as incubators, accelerators, universities, and chambers of commerce, so they can offer more effective and tailored support to impact entrepreneurs.

oper_nm: Consolidation of Best Corporate Development Practices in the Water and Sanitation Sector in Colombia
objtv: The Technical Cooperation's overall goal is to contribute to the improvement of the quality and sustainability of the urban water and sanitation services through the consolidation of the corporate development results in the water and sanitation sector in Colombia fostered by the operation "Comprehensive development Urban Water and Sewerage Companies in Colombia (CO-T1457)".

oper_nm: Technical cooperation for the structuring of urban and infrastructure projects related to habitat, building reuse, and housing generation
objtv: This technical cooperation (TC) aims to facilitate the structuring of catalytic urban projects in the main cities of Colombia, associated with habitat, building reuse, and housing generation through: (i) the development of land renewal activities in selected urban areas; (ii) the approval of new urban development and infrastructure projects by homeowners' associations; and (iii) analyzing the technical and financial prefeasibility to develop projects prioritized by local authorities, in accordance with the goals in the Development Plans and Territorial Ordinance Plans (POT).

oper_nm: Support to the structuring of a Just Energy Transition Platform
objtv: The main objective of this CT is to support the Government of Colombia in the structuring of a national Just Energy Transition Platform (JET), through: 1) technical studies to define the investment portfolio of the Colombian JET Platform and its contribution to Colombia's NDCs; 2) economic studies to analyze the benefits and impacts of the different dimensions of the JET at the sectoral and territorial level; and 3) design of recommendations about the necessary public policy and regulatory framework adjustments to promote an ambitious TEJ.

oper_nm: Technical support to strengthen the Social Prosperity Department’s Productive Inclusion Strategy
objtv: This Technical Cooperation (TC) aims to strengthen the institutional capacities of the Department of Social Prosperity (DPS) to formulate and implement its strategy for productive inclusion in Colombia. To achieve this, the TC will seek to: (i) provide technical support through economic, regulatory, and institutional capacity analyses to inform the design and implementation of the DPS's new tools for promoting productive inclusion, and to assess the technical, financial, and legal feasibility of these tools; (ii) produce a literature review and a comparative analysis of international best practices for productive inclusion; and (iii) create spaces for training, dialogue, and experience sharing on productive inclusion in Colombia.

oper_nm: Evolution of neocredit: better information, greater access for microentrepreneurs
objtv: Expand the access and use of Neocredito for Colombian micro-entrepreneurs and raise awareness among financial partners about the alternative use of data for their credit application evaluations.

oper_nm: Support for the development of the Social Household Registry in Colombia
objtv: The general objective of this technical cooperation is to support the National Planning Department in the implementation of the Social Household Registry. The specific objectives are: (i) strength the use of the household registry information at the national and local level; (ii) develop the single window for social services and the universal income registry; (iii) support the design of pilots of the single window in municipalities with different institutional development levels.

oper_nm: Are Conditions Still Important for Cash Transfers?
objtv: This TC will provide knowledge to address a strategic knowledge gap around the role of conditions in conditional cash transfers. While conditional cash transfers have been instrumental in alleviating poverty in the region, removing conditions that are no longer necessary could save the government monitoring costs. Further, the requirement to meet co-responsibilities may screen out some of the families most in need. Re-evaluating the impact of conditions will provide novel strategic knowledge to the Bank and its clients.

oper_nm: Strengthening the water and sanitation sector to improve service provision in Colombia
objtv: The Technical Cooperation's overall goal is to promote improved performance in the water and sanitation sector in Colombia, working both at the utility level and within public entities.

oper_nm: Evaluating the Role of Unpaid Care in the Rural Economy in Colombia
objtv: The objective of this TC is to measure the causal effect of a pilot initiative that includes the complementary investments in Rural Care Work in sustainable agricultural projects in Colombia, aimed at recognizing, reducing, redistributing, representing, and rewarding Rural Care Work activities. The evaluation will analyze the impact of these interventions on: (i) household income; (ii) food security; (iii) women's empowerment; (iv) women's workload; and (v) the performance of agricultural production activities. The specific objectives are: (i) to collect field data to measure the effects of the Rural Care Work pilot; (ii) to implement focus groups and other qualitative activities to thoroughly understand the analyzed effects; and (iii) to develop the impact evaluation of the complementary rural care work investments within the framework of the pilot.

oper_nm: Heal to Grow: Scaling Impact in Colombia
objtv: The proposed TC aims to develop and experimentally evaluate a highly scripted Heal to Grow outsourced early educator training model. The TC will contribute to the understanding the linkage between key execution issues and the effectiveness of education programs.

oper_nm: Knowledge Exchange between Colombia and Brazil on sharing experiences and best practices in urban planning in Curitiba as part of the 'Plan Cali 500+' project
objtv: The mission's objective is to exchange best practices in urban planning by studying the innovative strategies of Curitiba, particularly their long-term vision, public transportation, integrated urban development, and resilience planning. The mission aims to adapt these practices to Cali, with a focus on citizen participation, addressing contemporary urban challenges like climate change and socioeconomic inequality. The visit will also foster collaboration with local entities, securing co-financing for travel and accommodation, and strengthen technical cooperation between the Inter-American Development Bank and the "Plan Cali 500+" project.

oper_nm: Support for the Territorial Public Investment Strengthening Program
objtv: Support the necessary conditions in subnational governments and Findeter to increase public investment in infrastructure for the provision of public goods, services, and equipment in territorial entities in Colombia. This is done by strengthening the technical capacities of Findeter and the Territorial Entities to structure, evaluate, and support urban and territorial infrastructure projects with cross-cutting approaches to gender, diversity, energy efficiency, and carbon neutrality. This is also done by improving mechanisms for identifying and grouping eligible, high-priority projects in territories with lower capacities.

oper_nm: Artificial Intelligence models for congestion prediction and optimal traffic management in Bogotá
subsector_nm: DEMAND MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL OF URBAN TRANSPORT SYSTEMS
objtv: This Technical Cooperation (TC) aims to enhance traffic flow prediction and optimization in Bogotá by leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) as a key tool, utilizing existing data resources for traffic management and transportation planning, and establishing a clear pathway for AI integration into mobility management.

oper_nm: Zero deforestation cocoa: A model for sustainability and market access for agroforestry cocoa producers in the Colombian Amazon
objtv: The technical cooperation's objective is to strengthen the cocoa value chain in the Colombian Amazon through: (i) promoting georeferenced zero-deforestation traceability, (ii) encouraging the transition to biodiverse agroforestry systems (AFS) that increase productivity and diversify income, and (iii) fostering associative strengthening and commercial linkages.

oper_nm: Support the use of AI to generate efficiencies in the Colombian Healthcare System
objtv: The objective of this technical cooperation (TC) is to support the use of artificial intelligence to increase the efficiency of the General System of Social Security in Health (SGSS) in Colombia. To meet this objective, the TC will focus on i) assisting in the design and implementation of artificial intelligence tools based on models and algorithms for the auditing processes of health services and technologies, considering the ethical use of AI, ii) developing training sessions for the personnel of the Resource Administrator of the General Social Security Health System - ADRES - to promote the ethical and responsible use of artificial intelligence techniques and, iii) deploying experience exchange sessions with other countries.

oper_nm: Knowledge Exchange between the cities of Bogotá and Cali (Colombia) and Buenos Aires (Argentina) on Waste Management and Recycling Practices
objtv: The objective of this technical cooperation is to exchange best practices and experiences in comprehensive solid waste management between the city of Buenos Aires and Bogotá and Cali. This exchange encompasses aspects such as recycling, waste containerization, organic waste treatment, and collaboration with recycling cooperatives. The mission aims to identify innovative and adaptable solutions to enhance operational efficiency and environmental sustainability in both contexts.

oper_nm: Support for the Digital Transformation of Justice Agenda
objtv: This Technical Cooperation (TC) seeks to support the strengthening of institutional capacities in the Colombian justice sector, promoting the development of skills and advanced technologies that support the sector's digital transformation agenda. Specifically, this TC will support: (i) the development and implementation of governance strategies, information management systems, and the adoption of advanced technologies to improve judicial and administrative processes; (ii) the strengthening of digital capacities for the digital transformation of justice in Colombia; and (iii) knowledge management for Digital Justice.

oper_nm: Support the sustainability of Colombia's energy sector
subsector_nm: ENERGY INSTITUTIONAL STRENGTHENING AND CAPACITY BUILDING
objtv: The objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to support the strengthening of the sustainability of Colombia's electricity sector, including improvements to the subsidy targeting scheme and the promotion of individual self-generation strategies to protect electricity consumption for the most vulnerable users. The specific objectives are: (i) to support the sustainability of electricity service for vulnerable households through the analysis of public policy strategies that promote the closing of fiscal gaps in electricity subsidies, including improvements in subsidy targeting; (ii) to support the development of public policy measures that promote more affordable service and encourage the adoption of non-conventional renewable energies, including the Colombia Solar program, which promotes the installation of solar panels in low-income households; and (iii) to strengthen institutional capacities to improve the sector's sustainability.

oper_nm: Support to the Amazonian Region Energy Transition
objtv: The objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to support the Government of Colombia (GoC) in preparing a large-scale strategy for a Just Energy Transition (JET) in the Amazon region that promotes comprehensive development of the area and contributes to the achievement of the country's decarbonization goals.

oper_nm: Support for Integrated Migration Policy
objtv: The objective of this non-reimbursable technical cooperation is to support the Government of Colombia in the optimization of the Intégrate Centers' attention schemes, the inter-institutional coordination mechanisms, and in a strategy to guarantee the sustainability of attention to the migrant population. It will also support the implementation of activities and schemes to contribute to the prevention of smuggling of migrants in Colombia through the Intégrate Centers. These actions will contribute to the exercise of rights and protection of the migrant population, returnees and host communities, with special emphasis on migrants, as well as their socio-economic inclusion.

oper_nm: Support for advancing the agenda of trade logistics, investment, and productive and export development
subsector_nm: TRADE FACILITATION, TRADE LOGISTICS AND CUSTOMS
objtv: The general objective of this TC is to support the Government of Colombia, in particular the National Planning Department (DNP), in the implementation of the PNL investment loan (5229/OC-CO) and the program of policy reforms supporting Colombia's integration into the GVCs (5982/OC-CO). The specific objectives are:(i) to promote the execution, monitoring, evaluation, sustainability and closure of these operations; and (ii) to support the strengthening of the technical capacities of the DNP and other public entities involved in the implementation of this program agenda.

oper_nm: Support for the Institutional Strengthening and Modernization of FINAGRO
objtv: The objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to strengthen the institutional capacities of the Fund for the Financing of the Agricultural Sector (FINAGRO) to improve its efficiency in financing the Colombian agricultural sector. The specific objectives seek to strengthen FINAGRO's technical capabilities in the development of financial products, implementation of methodologies for impact measurement, and integration of sustainability criteria into its financing strategy, in order to promote sustainable and resilient agricultural development.

oper_nm: Support for the implementation of the national reference unit for genomic profile characterization and data management by the National Institute of Health
objtv: The objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to design, develop, and implement a national platform for genomic surveillance of microorganisms of public health interest in Colombia (VIGIPAT) under the responsibility of the National Institute of Health (INS).

oper_nm: Support for the Comprehensive Early Childhood Care Policy - Phase II
objtv: The objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to support the District Secretariat for Social Integration (SDIS) and the District Education Secretariat (SED) of Bogota in the design and implementation of the Comprehensive District System for Early Childhood Care (SDAIPI) through the development of its Nominal Monitoring System (SSN) and a quality assurance system for early childhood services. This TC provides programmatic continuity to activities in operations CO-T1770 (ATN/OC-21187-CO) and CO-R1007.

oper_nm: Country Platform for achieving climate and just energy transition goals: governance and portfolio
objtv: The objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to support the Government of Colombia in establishing the process of a Country Platform for a Just Energy Transition, as a mechanism for dialogue and collaboration with the international community to promote the achievement of Colombia's NDC climate goals under the Paris Agreement.

oper_nm: Promoting the Use and re-Use of Open Data in Colombia
objtv: The main objective of this technical cooperation is to support the government of Colombia, through the implementation of their open data initiatives, with emphasis on impactful activities related to the use and re-use of open data.

oper_nm: Support for the structuring of efficient and sustainable PPPs in the social sector in Colombia
objtv: The objective of this technical cooperation (TC) is to promote efficient, sustainable and responsible private investment in public social infrastructure in Colombia, such as health and education. This objective will be achieved though the implementation of feasibility and structuring studies to design Public Private Partnership Contracts that offers value for money for public sectors, that delivers quality service to users and that promotes a balance between risks and rentability to private sector investors. The TC will support public entities in Colombia, such as the National Infrastructure Agency, to conduct financial, technical, environmental and legal assessments that are required to prepare PPP contracts in the social sector in line with the countries National Development Plan

oper_nm: Development of Financing and Monitoring Mechanisms to support the Implementation of Colombia’s Biodiversity Action Plan
objtv: The objective of this TC is to support the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development in developing a technological platform to monitor investments in nature and advance the implementation of Colombia's Biodiversity Action Plan (NBSAP) targets. To achieve this, the initiative will strengthen governance and institutional capacity, facilitate the development of new regulatory frameworks, and promote agile methodologies for data integration. Additionally, it will support the creation of innovative financial mechanisms to mobilize public and private capital for biodiversity protection, aligning with the indicators and reporting processes of the Global Biodiversity Framework and Colombia's NBSAP.

oper_nm: Support for project preparation under the Colombia Country Platform
subsector_nm: ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND RENEWABLE ENERGY IN END USE
objtv: The objective of this TC is to support the Government of Colombia in the structuring of a Country Platform that supports compliance with the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and with a first phase focused on the Just Energy Transition (TEJ), including electromobility, through the definition and preparation of a sectoral portfolio of projects (especially electric regional train projects and electric bus projects in intermediate cities). Likewise, support will be given to the design of governance and financial instruments that will enable the viability of the projects.

oper_nm: Public-Private linkages to promote development of the Huétar Norte Region
objtv:
When local governments, universities, companies and business associations in a region decide to take concerted action with the goal of enhancing the growth of MSMEs operating in it, the chances of achieving significant results will grow exponentially. Not only that, when these actions incorporate strengthening of local competitive factors, the impact will be even greater, as they help to maximize the development potential of the region itself. 

This is the Local Economic Development (LED) approach that the MIF will support in the Huétar Norte Region of Costa Rica; a project that will showcase an emerging center of economic development as an example of what coordinated public-private linkages and actions can accomplish. This macro approach is a result of learning from over 30 projects the MIF has supported in the last 15 years, ranging from the provision of business development services to SMEs, to the promotion of business cluster development. 

In Huétar Norte, a region with two strategic sectors ¿food production and tourism- and many of the assets needed to spark development, but that also faces obstacles such as low level of industrialization, lack of a clearly defined business strategies and inadequate treatment of agricultural and industrial waste, the project will focus on strengthening public-private linkages to improve those territorial assets, and include over 500 MSMEs in the value chains by innovating their processes, products and services. The use of bio-controllers and traceability in agriculture and the reduction of the carbon footprint in tourism are just some examples of the project¿s featured activities. The Development Association of the Huétar Norte will be the MIF partner to carry out this ambitious initiative. 

Over the next four years, the project will generate practical knowledge and tools on how to effectively build a territorial governance mechanism among public-private stakeholders, how to strengthen partnerships and production linkages among MSMEs, and how to implement innovative and economically viable alternative for reuse and treatment of agricultural waste, critical for the environmental sustainability of the region. 

The potential for an impact beyond Huétar Norte Region looks quite promising as well. This experience will provide tangible and measurable results on how to carry out local economic development in a country like Costa Rica, thereby enriching policy dialogue with the Costa Rican local and central government officials, and with other countries in the region. The results can influence the development of MSME policies to incorporate a local productive perspective, and take into consideration requirements outside the capital city, to create policies and programs built on a common understanding of needs, limitations, assets and opportunities.

oper_nm: Support for the Implementation of Costa Rica's Gender Route

The specific objectives are: (i) Strengthen public-private partnerships through the gender parity initiative. (iii) Strengthen the institutional capacity of INAMU and give sustainability to the Violet Points and Safe Spaces of the GBV route within the framework of the gender route. oper_nm: Climate Risk Atlas for the Dominican Republic
objtv: This technical cooperation (TC) aims to support the Government of the Dominican Republic in the development and implementation of the country's national climate risk atlas, considering historical and future data and the climate change scenario. The atlas will contain information on the different climate threats that affect the country, the exposure and vulnerability to these events and the corresponding level of risk. The set of information generated will be hosted on a web platform that will allow dynamic visualization, interaction with the data and downloading of the information. The climate risk atlas will aim to support climate risk management, contribute to the land use planning process given the recent entry into force of the Land Use Planning Law, and serve as a key tool for the design of other public policies and resilient infrastructure. The specific objectives of the TC are: i) to carry out an inventory and systematization of the existing information in the country related to climate risk; ii) to update the country's future climate projections, for various shared socioeconomic trajectories (SSP), based on numerical models and taking into account existing data; iii) identify and characterize the country's main climate threats that have a high potential to impact the economy, essential infrastructure and human beings (droughts, floods, landslides, extreme winds, rising sea levels, etc.); iv) assess vulnerability, exposure and risk to these climate threats; v) develop a web platform that allows public access to the data generated. The country has made great progress in managing climate risks, but additional effort is needed, as reflected in the November 2013 Climate and Development Report of the Dominican Republic, prepared by the World Bank. This report highlights the need to improve information on threats, vulnerability and climate risks, as well as transparency and access to this information. This data constitutes a key tool for making informed decisions and developing better public policies for managing these risks. The climate atlas of the Dominican Republic will be a tool that directly or indirectly supports the formulation and improvement of various public policies, with the aim of promoting more resilient and sustainable development in a context of increasing climate change. Within this, it highlights the support in the process of territorial planning underway in the country, providing information on the risks associated with current and future climate phenomena.

oper_nm: Access to Markets for Afro-Ecuadorian Youth: The Quest for Economic Rights
objtv:
The objectives of this TC operation will be accomplished through the implementation of the following components: 1) Tuna Fruit production ; 2) Tuna fruit commercialization; and 3) Tuna fruit industrialization.
I. Production. The goal of this component is to increase and improve tuna production by: (i) establishing new tuna plantations; (ii) providing training and technical assistance to protect existing plantations, by improving soil fertility and facilitating transition towards sustainable agricultural practices; and (iii) providing training and technical assistance for tuna harvesting and post-harvesting. At the end of the project it is expected that families have improved their income. Project expected results are: 30 additional hectares of tuna fruit plantations established, 108 families applying sustainable agriculture techniques, and 108 families using improved tuna harvesting and post-harvesting techniques
II. Commercialization. The goal of this second component is to improve access to tuna fruit markets. This would be achieved by strengthening the "Tuna Producers Association of Ecuador" via training and technical assistance in legal affairs (to obtain legal status), management of micro-enterprises, marketing techniques, and business/financial planning. Emphasis would be given to promoting the associative commercialization of tuna fruit. At the end of the project it is expected that contacts have been established with at least 10 new potential tuna fruit buyers, and that the Tuna Producers Association would be legally established and commercializing tuna fruit associatively.
III: Feasibility study: The goal of this last component is to explore the possibilities of industrializing tuna products. This would be achieved by the commissioning of feasibility study that could identify new products, at least 3, and its potential markets.

oper_nm: Teacher Professional Development Program
objtv:
The general objective of this technical cooperation is to assist the Ecuadorian Ministry of Education in improving the quality of basic education for all children, but especially those from poor and disadvantaged backgrounds. The TC will achieve this by addressing one of the greatest challenges common to education systems of countries across Latin America and the world: how to improve the quality of in-service teachers in such a way as to directly improve student's learning outcomes. This operation builds on evidence generated by rigorous studies examining the impact of teacher quality on student learning outcomes, including the IDB's own groundbreaking longitudinal study, "Closing Gaps", which has further advanced the field of knowledge on the relationship between teaching practices and student learning. At a time when governments across Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) are searching for effective professional development strategies to improve teacher quality, the outcome of this TC – an evidence-based, field-tested mentoring package for in-service teachers along with implementation guidelines – will serve to not only inform policy in Ecuador but also to provide a concrete intervention specifically tailored for countries in the region.

The quality of an educational system depends in great part on the quality of its teachers. That said, in countries across Latin America and the world, most teachers fall far short of their potential to transform children's lives, and to date policy makers and governments have lacked the knowledge and tools to support in-service teachers in a way that produces improved student learning. To this end, the specific objective of this TC is to develop and pilot an evidence-based teacher professional development program providing ongoing mentoring for in-service elementary school teachers to directly improve their pedagogical practices. The pilot is unique in that it gives teachers individualized and specific support to improve practices in their classrooms, to have more effective interactions with their students, and to make the most out of their day-to-day classroom experiences to maximize student learning in an ongoing mentorship context. Furthermore, there is no evidence to date of any evidence-based, practical ongoing professional development programs aimed at improving teacher quality anywhere in all of Latin America and the Caribbean, and in this sense our project fills an urgent need and introduces an innovative and proven method for achieving this goal.

The pilot will culminate in a stand-alone mentoring package with step-by-step implementation protocols and training materials that can be implemented in any country in the region including Ecuador. This package will serve as a model for other countries – including more developed countries – to identify and train teachers to successfully become excellent mentors providing individualized, practical and ongoing support to their peers to improve everyday practices in their classrooms and in turn improve student learning.

oper_nm: Closing Gaps: The Medium-term Impacts of Teaching Quality in Primary School
objtv:
The general objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to continue the groundbreaking work of Closing Gaps. "Closing Gaps" is a longitudinal study in Ecuador collecting first-of-its-kind information on the relationship between teaching quality and children's learning in public elementary schools, and use the results to directly inform educational policy reform in the region. To this end, Closing Gaps has spent the past four years meticulously gathering and analyzing randomized control data from a cohort of Ecuadorian teachers and their students from the coastal region of the country, to identify the specific teacher characteristics and practices that allow young, disadvantaged children, who enter school with profound deficits in their cognitive development, to close their skills gaps and catch up to their peers as they advance through primary school. 

To this end, the TC has two specific objectives: (i) to generate evidence on learning outcomes from the cohort of students and teachers in the study during their 4th grade of elementary school, and (ii) to compare and analyze the results that have already been obtained from the project to determine whether the effects found of the impact of teacher quality on student learning are persistent over time and how they interact. These objectives will allow us to assess: (i) whether short-term teacher effects on children's learning and development observed after each year of schooling are maintained over time; (ii) how having a better teacher in one grade affects having a better teacher in the following grade;[1] (iii) whether teacher effects are stable from one year to another (Does teaching quality vary from year to year? Is a "good" teacher "good" across different school years? Is a teacher "good" with different groups of students?); and (iv) potential pilots of professional development interventions to increase teacher quality. This work will provide the foundation upon which policy makers in the region can build strong teacher policies to improve the delivery of high quality education.

oper_nm: Closing Gaps VI and VII: teaching and learning throughout primary school
objtv:
This TC will support the last stages of an innovative ongoing study in Ecuador, Closing Gaps. No study of teacher quality in a developing country is comparable in the rigorous design of its identification strategy, nor in its execution. The project's main objective is to better understand the learning process during elementary school, and to identify which of those characteristics and practices of teachers in the classroom are most successful in closing the learning gap between the poorest children and their better-off classmates. These effects can only be observed throughout time, and are the ones that provide the most meaningful evidence to inform policy. Hence, the Bank has been carrying out this unprecedented longitudinal study, about to enter its sixth year. In Closing Gaps, two cohorts of children entering kindergarten (in 2012 and 2013), totaling more than 24,000 students, were randomly assigned to different classrooms within 200 schools. Children from the 2012 cohort were then randomly reassigned to classrooms in 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th grade. In every grade, compliance with the assignment rule has been almost perfect.
This TC has two specific objectives: (i) to generate evidence on learning outcomes from the cohort of students and the effectiveness of teachers during the last two grades of elementary school; and (ii) to compare and analyze the results that have already been obtained throughout the project. 
This stage of Closing Gaps will be fundamental, as the data will be used to determine whether the effects of teacher quality on student learning are persistent in time during the entire elementary school cycle, and more importantly, to improve the understanding of how these effects interact differently with student learning from one year to the next during these extremely important formative years. The analysis of the results of this last phase will yield unparalleled information that the region has never had at its disposal before. Some of the questions that we will be able to answer include: Could a child assigned to an ineffective teacher in one year eventually catch up with a child that was assigned to an effective teacher that same year? Or would the child assigned to an effective teacher also learn more in all subsequent primary school years? Which different sequences of "effective" and "ineffective" teachers, during elementary school, matter more or less for a child's learning? To generate answers that could be applicable to the entire elementary school in general, and grade by grade in particular, it is necessary to obtain data of these last two years in elementary school (5th & 6th grade) of the children in the sample.
The project has significant and direct policy implications for Ecuador and other countries in the region, by providing rigorous evidence for the design of effective teacher selection and evaluation systems, targeted in-service teacher training programs, and for compensatory educational programs for disadvantaged children, among others. The first results of the project have been used in the design of an approved loan (EC-L1155), in the ongoing dialogue on early schooling and teaching quality with other countries of the region, and disseminated in a number of seminars and conferences. The results of the first year and a half of the project were published in a highly recognized peer reviewed journal in Economics (QJE), and a series of working papers with the rest of the results are currently in production.

oper_nm: Closing Gaps: Teaching and Learning Math in the Early Grades
objtv:
Early math achievement is critical, but what determines how much math young children learn and how can math achievement be improved? This Technical Cooperation seeks to build upon the groundbreaking study in Ecuador, Closing Gaps, to answer that question. Closing Gaps began at the request of the Government of Ecuador in 2012, when an incoming cohort of approximately 15,000 kindergarten children in 202 schools was randomly assigned to their teachers. These children have been randomly re-assigned to teachers year after year in their 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th grades, meaning that Closing Gaps offers a truly unique opportunity to answer some of the most pressing questions about how to improve student mathematics learning. In no country, developed or developing, has there been an experiment that randomly assigned children to teachers in multiple grades. 

Specifically, this TC will answer a number of very important questions that both directly and indirectly impact mathematics learning and teaching in elementary school, and will be of great practical use to policy makers in the region. Among them, do children who had a better math teacher in, say, kindergarten or first grade have higher math scores upon graduation from elementary school? Does having a better math teacher in 1st grade matter more or less than having a better math teacher in 4th grade? Are children who had better elementary math teachers more likely to continue on to secondary school? Is the total cumulative effect of having two good teachers greater than the simple sum of the effects of those two individual teachers? Under what circumstances are teachers effective in ensuring that girls, whose math achievement lags behind that of boys, learn math skills? The answers to these questions will allow for more effective and precise policies to improve math learning and teaching in Ecuador and throughout Latin America.
Furthermore, this TC will collect data to compare how math is taught in different classrooms and identify the most effective practices for optimizing student learning. Do teachers who spend more time in intentional, focused math teaching (relative to teaching other subjects) produce more math learning? What is the optimal amount of time spent teaching basic math computations (like addition or subtraction) as opposed to developing children's deeper understanding of math concepts? 
The questions to be answered by this TC have never before been rigorously investigated in Latin America. Not only does the TC offer a unique opportunity to understand how young children learn and how to best support their teachers, but these questions have significant and direct implications for pre-service and in-service teacher training, and for curriculum design.

La EPMMQ fue creada en 2012 como agencia pública a cargo de la gerencia del proyecto y desde abril de 2016, se dió el inicio a los trabajos, actualmente con avance de ejecución del 25%. Es importante señalar que el BID a través de sus operaciones EC-L1111 y EC-L1124 financia US$200 millones, contando con financiamiento paralelo de otras entidades multilaterales: Banco Europeo de Inversiones, Corporación Andina de Fomento y Banco Mundial, para un monto total aproximado de proyecto de US$ 2010 millones.

Con la ejecución de la PLMQ se busca mejorar la movilidad urbana en la ciudad de Quito atendiendo la creciente demanda de transporte público. A través de su implementación, el objetivo es reducir los tiempos de viaje, los costos operacionales del servicio de transporte, mejorar la conectividad de la red de transporte, seguridad, el confort del actual sistema y reducir las emisiones de contaminantes y gases de efecto invernadero. Bajo los programas de préstamo EC-L1111, EC-L1124 y la nueva operación EC-L1222 se ejecutarán 23 km de línea, 15 estaciones, un patio de cocheras con área de mantenimiento, arquitectura y adecuación del sistema, y se proveerá el material móvil compuesto por 18 trenes de 6 vagones cada uno. 

Si bien esta CT se centrará en temas institucionales, contribuye integralmente con el préstamo a las siguientes metas del GCI-9: "préstamo a países pequeños y vulnerables" y "protección al medio ambiente", en especial a través del desarrollo del adecuado modelo de gestión ambiental que se prevé financiar.

A través de la CT previa EC-T1260, el Banco apoyó a la EPMMQ para que pueda desarrollarse como institución desde su nivel incipiente hacia una mayor eficiencia en su desempeño institucional durante la ejecución de la obra. En el marco de esta cooperación se financiaron las siguientes actividades: i) modelo de explotación de la PLMQ: consultoría para el desarrollo de la propuesta del modelo de explotación de la PLMQ, modelo de control de gestión para la administración de los contratos de Fase 2 de la PLMQ y contratación de servicios de asesoría legal contrato FIDIC y resolución de conflictos. ii) gestión ambiental, social y de seguridad ocupacional: contratación de expertos en gestión social y ambiental, así como el diseño e implementación del sistema de información para la gestión ambiental, social y de seguridad y salud Ocupacional, diseño e implementación de un programa de fortalecimiento a negocios en el área de influencia de la PLMQ.

oper_nm: Closing Gaps: Household Evidence and Behavior Assessment
objtv:
The objective of this Technical Cooperation is to collect data about the environments to which students are exposed to, including household composition, socioeconomic status, and other relevant variables that might affect student development. Furthermore, this Technical Cooperation will also gather information regarding student's behavior from the students' households through the use of various instruments such as the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) which can capture the psychosocial perspective of children and young people, their parents and teachers. This tool considers five areas including emotional symptoms, conduct problems, hyperactivity/inattention, peer relationship problems and prosocial behavior to assess the psychological adjustment of children and youth in different households. This data will be used to study the relationship between household behavior and school learning.

This TC will support the last stages of an innovative ongoing study in Ecuador, Closing Gaps. No study of teacher quality in a developing country is comparable in the rigorous design of its identification strategy, nor in its execution. The main objective for this stage of the project is to collect data through surveys regarding student's household factors to understand how different household variables affect student learning and children's behavior. These effects can only be observed throughout time and are the ones that provide the most meaningful evidence to inform policy. Hence, the Bank has been carrying out this unprecedented longitudinal study, about to enter its sixth year. In Closing Gaps, two cohorts of children entering kindergarten (in 2012 and 2013), totaling more than 24,000 students, were randomly assigned to different classrooms within 200 schools. Children from the 2012 cohort were then randomly reassigned to classrooms in 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th grade. In every grade, compliance with the assignment rule has been almost perfect. This TC has two specific objectives: (i) to collect the necessary data using various instruments such as the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) regarding the conditions of different households from all the participant students and ; and (ii) to compare, assess and provide a thorough analysis of the collected data that generates substantial evidence on the effects of household inputs in student learning outcomes and behavior patterns and the impacts that these factors could possibly have in the students' adult life.

objtv: Support the institutional strengthening of the Empresa Pública Metropolitana Metro de Quito (EPMMQ) to improve its technical and management capacity in providing the operational service of the First Line of the Quito Metro (PLMQ), assess the impact of its operation, contribute to enhancing its integration with other transportation systems, and its strategic planning for future projects.

oper_nm: Medium Term Fiscal Strategy
subsector_nm: FISCAL POLICY FOR SUSTAINABILITY AND GROWTH
objtv: Support the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) in the preparation of a medium-term fiscal reform and a country growth agenda, which results in improving the country's fiscal resilience and reactivating economic growth in a sustainable manner.

oper_nm: Support for the competitive, inclusive, and sustainable internationalization of Ecuador
objtv: The primary objective of this TC is to support the Government of Ecuador in implementing the National Investment Attraction and Facilitation System loan (EC-L1243, 4754/OC-EC), while also promoting more effective utilization of the country's trade agreements. This support aims to facilitate a more competitive, inclusive, and sustainable internationalization of Ecuador. The specific objectives include: (i) enhancing the country's commercial integration and investment attraction strategy; and (ii) strengthening the domestic agenda to reduce transaction costs and enhance the productive and export capacities of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), with a focus on gender.

oper_nm: Technical support to reinforce the implementation of the improved national multi-threat early warning system
objtv: Support for the strengthening and consolidation of the Risk Management Secretariat in its role of coordinating the National Early Warning System (EWS) for multiple hazards in Ecuador.

oper_nm: Support for the sustainable development of housing and the urban sector in Ecuador
objtv: To promote the adoption of strategies that contribute to sustainable and climate-resilient development from the housing and urban development sector in Ecuador through the empowerment and articulation of key actors, capacity building, the identification and promotion of cost-efficient strategies and the development of tools that facilitate the implementation and monitoring of these strategies.

oper_nm: Optimization of public management with a focus on the quality of results, ensuring coordination between subnational governments and the central government
objtv: The objective is to contribute to strengthening institutional capacity and improving public management of municipalities, as strategic local entities, focusing on enhancing monitoring and evaluation tools, the quality of results and expenditures, subnational fiscal sustainability, and horizontal and vertical coordination, in order to generate development opportunities and promote the welfare of citizens.

oper_nm: Institutional Strengthening for the development of an Integral Security Policy in Ecuador
objtv: Strengthen the capabilities of security sector entities and the country to improve their management, particularly in areas of prevention, control, security, and citizen coexistence, prioritizing a gender and diversity approach, as well as the prevention of violence and crime. This will be achieved through specialized technical assistance, knowledge exchange, and the implementation of best practices learned from regional and international experiences, in coordination with subnational governments interested in Ecuador.

oper_nm: Natural Capital: An alternative for the sustainable development of Yasuní
objtv: The objective of this operation is to value natural capital as an alternative for the sustainable development of Yasuní, strengthening the bioeconomy and working with communities for the construction of Yasuní Nature Positive, a project that is part of the national initiative called Amazon Biocorridor and that views integrate the economic valuation of biodiversity and ecosystem services with the worldview and cultural sense of the Waorani community through the Waorani Nationality of Ecuador, NAWE.

oper_nm: Highly skilled human resources in ICT and research lines relevant to threats of climate change in the Galapagos Islands
objtv: Identify undergraduate and graduate programs, as well as research lines at ESPOL, whether new or existing, that can engage in activities at an institution campus in the Galapagos Islands and contribute to the sustainable development of the Islands. The specific objectives are: (i) strengthen the academic offerings for third and fourth-level education in the Islands, and (ii) generate knowledge to address the social, cultural, and environmental challenges of the island system and the sustainable management of the archipelago's natural resources.

oper_nm: Support for Universal Access to Electricity in the Ecuadorian Amazon and Institutional Strengthening for a Just and Sustainable Energy Transition
objtv: Support universal access to electricity services in the Ecuadorian Amazon and strengthen institutions to advance a just and sustainable energy transition. The specific objectives are: (i) to finance feasibility studies for rural electrification projects in isolated areas, including the integration of bioeconomy principles and the design of photovoltaic and storage systems; (ii) to evaluate and optimize existing rural electrical systems, promoting the transition from fossil fuels to solar energy and developing an improvement plan; (iii) to develop a comprehensive roadmap for the implementation of inclusive electrical systems, prioritizing gender equity and diversity; and (iv) to strengthen institutional and regulatory capacities, supporting the publication of sectoral statistics, the development of the Andean Short-Term Electricity Market (MAERCP), and the implementation of gender strategies in the sector.

oper_nm: Supporting the educational transformation in Ecuador
objtv: The objective of this technical cooperation is to support the Ministry of Education of Ecuador in its educational transformation plan. Technical support focuses on both pedagogical issues, such as the new curriculum reform implemented by the Ministry, and management aspects, for example, improving the monitoring processes of educational resources at the local level, especially the allocation of teachers. Additionally, this technical cooperation will provide support to the National Institute of Educational Evaluation to improve the production of data on educational quality in Ecuador in order to inform policies that will drive educational transformation in the country.

oper_nm: Knowledge Exchange between Ecuador and Chile on Operational, Maintenance, and Organizational Models for Metro Systems
subsector_nm: PUBLIC TRANSPORT (BUS / TRAIN / CABLE). INFRASTRUCTURE AND EQUIPMENT
objtv: The purpose of the technical visit is to conduct a technical exchange with other metro systems in the region to learn about best practices in operational management and institutional strengthening, which will contribute to the improvement of operational, maintenance, and non-fare revenue generation systems for the Quito Metro.

oper_nm: Knowledge exchange between Ecuador and Uruguay on programs to promote research, innovation and governance with the private sector in the agricultural sector
objtv: The purpose of the technical visit is to learn about the best practices of the National Institute of Agricultural Research of Uruguay (NIAR) and other similar institutions in governance and the involvement of the private sector and academia as strategic partners in decision-making for research, development, and innovation (R&D&I) policy in the agricultural sector.

oper_nm: Knowledge Exchange between Ecuador and Colombia on operation and maintenance management of wastewater treatment plants and corporate governance
objtv: Visiting Empresas Públicas de Medellín and Empresa de Acueducto y Alcantarillado de Bogotá to learn about the experience in the operation and maintenance management of wastewater treatment plants and corporate governance.

oper_nm: Fair and inclusive Energy Transition in Ecuador
objtv: The objective is to support the execution and implementation of the policy measures by the GoE toward a just energy transition and the promotion of investments in Ecuador's energy sector. The specific objectives are: (i) to support a series of actions to achieve an orderly, fair, and inclusive energy transition, including (a) building capacity and developing skills about the energy transition in public and private sector actors, and tools to reach agreements between the actors that intervene in territories with energy activities, (b) developing a strategy to eliminate barriers to investment in the energy transition and identify opportunities in the value chain, from mining production to renewable energy generation, (c) strengthening planning tools for expanding the electricity transmission sector during the energy transition, and (d) developing efficient business schemes to create an investment plan for providing clean and affordable electricity to communities currently lacking such services; (ii) to design and implement pilot projects with microgrid solutions, individual solar energy systems, and other decentralized energy solutions, providing local technical training programs on rural and indigenous communities focused on isolated territories in the Amazon, and evaluating the sustainability of the projects; and (iii) to implement gender and disability strategies and actions, including: (a) workplace capacity building, (b) supporting community economic empowerment projects and cooking alternatives with a focus on women's access to energy in Amazonian territories, and (c) implementing infrastructures and innovations for women and people with disabilities in the energy sector, in accordance with the actions of the National Government.

oper_nm: Knowledge exchange on public policy for the development of cultural and creative industries
objtv: The objective of technical cooperation is to institutionally strengthen the development, implementation and evaluation of public policies to promote the creative economy, which will serve to create the Cultural and Creative Industries Law of Ecuador.

oper_nm: Strengthening institutional capacities for public-public and public-private coordination through Executive Committees
objtv: The objective of this Technical Cooperation is to strengthen the institutional capacities of the Ministry of Production, Foreign Trade, Investments, and Fisheries (MPCEIP) to promote and enhance conditions for the development of productive sectors. The specific objectives are: (i) to create and strengthen public and private institutional capacities necessary to articulate a policy of Sectoral Executive Boards (MES); (ii) to support the implementation of policy solutions to competitiveness issues identified in the MES; and (iii) to promote monitoring and impact evaluation of resulting policy actions.

oper_nm: Kara Solar, Deploying Solar Canoes in the Amazon Region
objtv: The objective of this project is to accelerate the deployment of solar powered river transportation in the Ecuadorian Amazon by developing new circular business models to drive commercialization, local assembly and manufacturing capacity to bring to market equipment built for Amazon conditions, and local indigenous technical services teams capable to install, maintain and guarantee the infrastructure.

oper_nm: Iche - Young People Cooking the Future: Promoting Ecuador’s Gastronomic Ecosystem
objtv: The objective of the project is to strengthen the gastronomic innovation ecosystem in Manabí through the creation of the Instituto Superior Técnico Iche (IST Iche). IST Iche will contribute to increasing adequate employment for vulnerable youth in Manabí by providing socio-emotional and technical training related to the Manabí gastronomic culture.

oper_nm: Support the preparation of the Water and Sanitation Programme for the city of Cuenca
objtv: The objective of the TC is to support the preparation and execution of the Water and Sanitation Program for the city of Cuenca (EC-L1297). Specifically, TC resources will be used to support: (i) the review and adjustment of project designs to be financed by the program, including complementary studies (economic, socio-environmental and climate change) that may be necessary for project implementation; (ii) the preparation, prioritization and definition of the ETAPA management improvement component; and (iii) the detailed planning of activities and the start-up of program implementation.

oper_nm: Humanitarian Assistance for population affected by heavy rains in municipalities of Penipe and Baños in Ecuador
objtv: The aim of this emergency technical cooperation is to offer humanitarian support to the Government of Ecuador in addressing the crisis caused by flooding and landslides due to heavy rainfall in the cantons of Baños de Agua Santa and Penipe. This assistance is intended to partially mitigate the emergency situation currently affecting these regions.

oper_nm: Cultivating Innovation in the Amazon: The Canopy Bridge Food Lab
objtv: The overall objective of this project is to develop new commercial food products, increase sales, and enhance farmer capacity in order to boost purchases of macambo, cassava, and other products from farmers.

oper_nm: Sustainability of the IDB financed longitudinal randomized control trial “Closing Gaps”
objtv: The objective of this TC is to ensure the long-term sustainability and continued relevance of the "Closing Gaps" project by maintaining updated participant information, gathering new data on critical social and economic topics, and generating policy-relevant research on the impact of educational quality on labor market outcomes and crime-related attitudes and behaviors. The specific objectives of the TC are: (i) Ensure the sustainability of CG. The importance to the Bank of ensuring that this project is sustained for the foreseeable future stems from the unique information that the project can provide, on the impact of classroom characteristics in elementary school on medium- and long-term variables, and the correlations over time among a vast number of characteristics of vulnerable children, adolescents and young adults along their lifetime. Having this information places the Bank in an inimitable position to provide policy-relevant evidence for Ecuador and the broader Latin American and the Caribbean region. (ii) Collect new information on key topics related to labor market participation, exposure/participation in crime activities, risky behaviors, migration, domestic violence and teen pregnancy. (iii) Conduct research to address critical questions regarding the impact of classroom quality, and other correlates, on medium- and long-term outcomes, including initial labor market conditions (e.g. first job or initial wages) and exposure or participation in criminal activities.

oper_nm: Support for the structuring, implementation and replicability of the Facility to Support the Renewable Energy Transition (fastER)
objtv: The objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to strengthen institutional capacities and develop the necessary skills to support the structuring and implementation of guaranteed operations for renewable energy projects (ERNC). The specific objectives of this TC are: (i) to strengthen the capacities of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) for the legal and financial structuring of guaranteed operations for ERNC projects; (ii) to strengthen socio-environmental supervision capacities for ERNC projects; and (iii) to facilitate the replicability of the structure through knowledge management and dissemination activities.

oper_nm: Understanding the impacts of metro systems in LAC: The case of Quito’s First Metro Line
subsector_nm: PUBLIC TRANSPORT (BUS / TRAIN / CABLE). INFRASTRUCTURE AND EQUIPMENT
objtv: This Technical Cooperation aims to evaluate the impact of Quito's First Metro Line (PLMQ by its initials in Spanish) on mobility, environmental, and socioeconomic outcomes. By generating rigorous causal evidence, this TC seeks to enhance the understanding of how large-scale transportation systems create societal value, providing insights to inform future projects of a similar nature across Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC).

oper_nm: COICA: Implementation of the Amazonia for Life Fund
objtv: This project aims to facilitate the structuring and execution of resources from the Amazonia for Life Fund (ALF) at the territorial level and to implement the governance of the Fund. To achieve this, the Technical Cooperation (TC) will support the Coordinator of Indigenous Organizations of the Amazon Basin (COICA) by providing institutional and technical preparation for the effective management of projects identified through the beneficiary indigenous organizations in each of the participating Amazonian countries, as well as by mobilizing additional financial resources for the ALF.

oper_nm: Knowledge Exchange between Peru and Ecuador on Programs to Promote Access to Internal Control System
objtv: The objective of this knowledge exchange is to learn about the good results of the implementation of the internal control system of the Peruvian Comptroller General's Office and lessons learned from the implementation of the control service model.

oper_nm: Boosting productive development in the Autonomous Decentralized Governments
objtv: Promote productive development in the Autonomous Decentralized Governments (GAD) through increasing the added value of local production and integrating into local and global value chains, incorporating environmental sustainability criteria.

oper_nm: Institutional and Technical Strengthening for the Sustainable and Resilient Management of Road Infrastructure in Ecuador
objtv: Support the institutional strengthening of the Ministry of Transport and the Development Bank of Ecuador to improve the management of both state and provincial road infrastructure, promoting safe, sustainable, and climate-resilient infrastructure, complementing the existing loans EC-L1295 and EC-L1289.

oper_nm: Support for the Development of Agricultural Public Services in Ecuador (DAPS)
objtv: The objective of technical cooperation (TC) is to support the preparation of the program "Support for the Development of Agricultural Public Services in Ecuador" (EC-L1303), which will be co-executed by INIAP and AGROCALIDAD, hereinafter referred to as "the Program," and has been agreed upon with the Government of Ecuador through the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF). The program aims to support the development of Ecuador's agricultural public services to improve the sector's competitiveness and agricultural exports. The TC will support the completion of studies (diagnostics and evaluations), action plans, training, and consultancies that will help define priority investments and create the necessary capacities for the monitoring and evaluation of the main results of the Program, as well as the preparation of the annexes required for the loan document. Additionally, it will finance actions to launch the implementation of the loan operation with both institutions.

oper_nm: Promoting behavioral changes in drinking water and sanitation in rural areas in Ecuador
objtv: The objective of this CT is to design and implement innovative water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) interventions through the social arts to promote behavioral changes that increase the sustainable use of WASH systems in the canton of Portoviejo and the canton of Cuenca. The intervention area may be extended to other cantons of the RoE if resources for Portoviejo and Cuenca are viable, creating economies of scale.

oper_nm: Humanitarian Assistance for population affected by forest fires and drought in Ecuador
objtv: The aim of this emergency technical cooperation is to offer humanitarian support to the Government of Ecuador in addressing the emergency caused by forest fires and severe drought conditions in several provinces of the country. This assistance is intended to partially mitigate the emergency situation currently affecting these regions.

oper_nm: Support for the implementation of social protection and labor markets projects in Ecuador
objtv: The general objective of this TC is supporting the Ecuadorian Government to improve employability through skills development in the Amazon region and contribute to the design of a National Care System in Ecuador.

oper_nm: Technical Support for the Implementation of the Security and Justice Agenda in Ecuador
objtv: The general objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to contribute to the institutional strengthening of Ecuador's citizen security and justice agencies to combat organized crime. Specifically, it aims to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of prevention, surveillance, intelligence, and investigation systems against organized crime, as well as to strengthen the institutional response to contain environmental crimes and mitigate their socio-environmental damages in the Ecuadorian Amazon.

oper_nm: Support to mitigate the energy crisis and financing of resilient electricity grids
objtv: The General Objective is to support the Government of Ecuador (GoE) in mitigating the impacts of the energy crisis on the country's productivity and competitiveness through: (i) strengthening regulation to facilitate private capital investment in the transmission sector and innovative technologies such as storage; (ii) improving the enabling environment for private investment in the generation and transmission sector; and (iii) developing a proposal for an electric market model for the country.

oper_nm: Strengthening state capacities to execute key functions of public administration
objtv: The objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to contribute to strengthening the institutional capacity of the State, aimed at improving the effectiveness in carrying out cross-cutting functions of public administration such as government oversight, public procurement, access to justice, among others, ensuring efficiency, effectiveness, and transparency in the use of public resources and promoting coordination among different systems with a view toward their interoperability.

oper_nm: Financing of Amazonian production chains through Corporacion Financiera Nacional
objtv: Support the implementation of the new CFN operation for 2025 aimed at large and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) within export production chains, which will launch a pilot financing program for SMEs operating in the Amazon.

oper_nm: Support to the Ministry of Economy and Finance in the execution and monitoring of EC-U0007
objtv: The objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to support the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), in its capacity as executing agency of the EC-U0007 guarantee operation, in its efforts to oversee the measures approved in the EC-U0007 Policy Matrix and the environmental commitments assumed by the Government of Ecuador that are backed by the IDB2 guarantee.

objtv: Action Plan C&D.

oper_nm: Knowledge exchange between Ecuador and Uruguay on technical, operational and administrative capacities for the development of public policy in competitiveness, technology and innovation
objtv: The objective is institutional strengthening in the development, implementation, and evaluation of public policies to promote production, entrepreneurship, innovation, and knowledge in the Prefectures of Guayas and Imbabura.

oper_nm: Operational support for achieving the goals of the sustainable nutrition development program in Ecuador
objtv: The objective of the operation is to support the Republic of Ecuador in the implementation of the Sustainable Nutrition Development Program in Ecuador. The specific objectives are: (i) to support the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) in structuring the sustainability-based financing instrument; and (ii) to support the Ministry of Public Health (MSP) in implementing actions to reduce chronic child malnutrition in health facilities and communities across Ecuador.

oper_nm: Governance, Sustainable Development, and Bioeconomy Rooted in Amazonian Indigenous Knowledge
objtv: Strengthen the Indigenous economy and governance of Ecuador's Amazonian Indigenous peoples by valuing their ancestral knowledge and utilizing complementary technologies, ensuring the sustainable management of their territories.

oper_nm: Development of the National Museum of Ecuador
objtv: The main objective is to assess the overall impact that would be achieved in Ecuador through the construction and digitalization of the National Museum of Ecuador, strengthening the role of culture as a cross-cutting pillar of development and serving as a regional pilot project with potential for replication.

oper_nm: Implementation of impact evaluation of the job skills certification program in Ecuador
objtv: The objective of technical cooperation is to support the Ministry of Labor of Ecuador in carrying out the implementation of the impact assessment of the labor competencies program of the Support for Commitment to Employment program for the Effectiveness of Employment Policies funded by the BID EC-L1284 credit project.

oper_nm: Too Good to Waste: Structuring the Quito Environmental Complex with private sector participation — a key strategy to mitigate methane emissions and advance toward a circular economy
objtv: Carry out the structuring of the Quito Environmental Complex Project, which consists of the design, financing, construction, operation, and maintenance of the infrastructure for the provision of the public service of comprehensive management of non-hazardous solid waste and residues in its phases of collection, transfer, treatment, recovery, valorization, and final disposal. The project aims to accelerate the transformation from linear solid waste management to a circular economy, reducing environmental impacts and methane emissions caused by this activity (2.5).

oper_nm: Preventing Youth Crime Involvement
objtv: The objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to support the Government of Ecuador in strengthening citizen-centered public policy and institutional responses to prevent youth involvement in organized crime. Specifically, it aims to generate rigorous evidence by assessing the effectiveness of a series of programs implemented by the Ministries of Education and Interior to prevent adolescent recruitment by criminal organizations. The TC will assess whether these programs reduce recruitment attempts, improve school safety, and enhance educational and psychosocial outcomes for students in high-crime areas.

oper_nm: BioAgroTech Innovation Hub
objtv: The objective of the project is to consolidate a BioAgro Tech Innovation Hub in Ecuador that brings together academia, businesses, and communities to accelerate the transfer and adoption of agricultural and biotechnological solutions, strengthening investment, productive inclusion of small producers and SMEs, and the development of high value-added ventures.

oper_nm: Knowledge Exchange between Argentina and Ecuador on the Criminal Defense Model of the Chilean Public Defender's Office
objtv: Understand the criminal defense model of Argentina's Public Defender's Office (DPP), covering its organizational structure and governance, case management and technical defense model, litigation strategies and performance in hearings, physical infrastructure and support technology platforms, training and human talent development policies, and its quality measurement systems and key performance indicators (KPIs). Exchange experiences on institutional challenges and advances through the presentation of the management model and modernization vision of Ecuador's Public Defender's Office (DPE), in order to establish a comparative and constructive dialogue. Identify best practices, management models, and lessons learned that are transferable or adaptable to the Ecuadorian reality in order to strengthen its mission capabilities, including the perspective of front-line public defenders on their tools and daily challenges, and direct observation of the application of oral litigation techniques in hearings.

oper_nm: PDF-A Conservation and Management of Sharks
objtv:
The project will develop a coordination mechanism between the Subseretary for Fisheries Resources (Ministry of Trade, Industrilisation, Fisheries and Competitiveness) and The Subsecretary for Natural Capital (Ministry of Environment). It will also establish an intersectorial working group that includes decision makers and managers, fishermen and NGOs representatives, is established to steer and drive the development and implementation of the NPOA-Sharks. This group will be established through an inter-ministerial agreement and will have clear terms of references and coordination mechanisms. 

The Project will also identify gaps in the knowledge about biological, landing and trade of sharks that are priority for decision making on management measures and actions to overcome them. The first step needed is to compile and analyse this information, together with the management framework for shark conservation and management and identify gaps and loopholes both on the technical and legal side. 

Third, the project will produce a GEF medium size project proposal that aims at (a) generating critical information needed for management decisions on shark fisheries and (b) further developing and implement the Ecuadorian NPOA-Sharks.

oper_nm: Support for the design and implementation of quality early childhood development models in El Salvador
objtv:
The objective of this technical cooperation is to support the Government of El Salvador in strengthening the quality and diversification of care services, including early childhood development (ECD) , through the development of new models of care, quality standards, and strengthening of the competencies of direct care staff. The technical cooperation supports the execution of subcomponent 2.2 of the project "Social Protection Responsive to Crashes in El Salvador" (ES-L1159). oper_nm: Support to the digital infrastructure in El Salvador
objtv: The general objective of this Technical Cooperation (TC) is to support the Government of El Salvador in strengthening governance and building the information technology infrastructure (data center) necessary to improve the administration, storage, availability, and sovereignty (security) of State data. This will ensure the widespread availability of public services to citizens and the extensive use of information exchange systems among public entities through the creation of the Government's Private Cloud. The specific objectives are: (i) to assess the storage and data management needs of 100% of the national government entities; (ii) to define the National Data Governance Strategy, centralization, and redundancy of State Data; (iii) to identify the technical and financial needs, as well as develop the conceptual, preliminary, and executive design for the project for El Salvador Data Center; (iv) to design the State's VPN (Virtual Private Network) to strengthen the information exchange system between State Entities and Organizations; and (v) to structure sustainability strategies for connectivity and service provision for educational, health, and security establishments.

oper_nm: IDB CLIMA - Climate resilience and Strengthening Education Pathways
objtv: This technical coperation has the objective of support the IDB CLIMA pilot program in El Salvador, with the strengthening of the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology (MINEDUCYT) and the Municipality Works Entity (DOM), as well as support with feasibility studies.
